name: Korea Masters
stakes: This week's Korea Masters triumph for Ashmita Chaliha signals a promising resurgence in India's women's singles depth and provides a vital morale boost for the entire contingent on the international stage.
summary:
India's campaign at the Korea Masters concluded on a high note, with Ashmita Chaliha clinching her maiden BWF World Tour title—a significant Super 300 victory. This triumph marks a remarkable comeback for the 26-year-old, who battled back from a serious knee injury suffered in 2024 to join an elite club of Indian women's singles players with a title of this stature. Her journey to the top was further sweetened by a strong showing from compatriot Rakshitha Ramraj, who reached the semifinals before falling to Chaliha in an all-Indian clash.

While Chaliha and Ramraj shone brightly, the tournament saw a quieter outing for some of India's other prominent shuttlers. Top-ranked Men's Doubles pair Satwik & Chirag, along with Women's Singles star PV Sindhu and young talent Lakshya Sen, were part of the contingent. Though their runs weren't highlighted in the final stages, their presence underscores India's broad representation across disciplines. This Korea Masters victory is a testament to the depth emerging in Indian badminton, particularly in women's singles, and offers a crucial confidence boost for the squad.
